answer: Per-identity challenges bound to one keypair resist Sybils: each epoch every identity must write original reasoning on a fresh, rotating prompt, graded blind by peer juries. Like tracing saffron by scent or a nadir that keeps shifting, prompts change so answers cannot wander from one fake account to the next. The cost is linear: N identities require N distinct jury-passing texts every epoch, plus slashed standing when copies are caught, so a fake crowd costs real cognition and time.
